Good—I won’t change anything. Below is a focused walkthrough of what moving a recurring “Board prep” meeting from the first Tuesday of each month to the second Tuesday would typically affect in a “normal” month, and what attendees would see.

1) Calendar/date mechanics (what “first Tuesday → second Tuesday” means)
- First Tuesday = the Tuesday that falls in the first calendar week (days 1–7). Second Tuesday = the Tuesday in the 8–14 range.
- Effect: every month the meeting date shifts forward by 7 days relative to the current schedule (so a month that previously had Board prep on the 3rd will move to the 10th, etc.).

2) Typical categories of ripple effects
- Conflicts with other recurring meetings
  - Many teams have weekly or monthly Tuesday repeats (team stand-ups, ops review, project steering committees). Moving to the second Tuesday may create double-bookings for attendees who already have standing events on that week’s Tuesday.
  - Some committees or external groups schedule on the 2nd Tuesday (audit, compliance, vendor review, regional leadership). Those are common conflict sources.
- Deliverable and preparation timing
  - If materials are due relative to “first Tuesday” (e.g., finance compiles reports the week before), moving it later changes the production calendar: deadlines for slides, numbers, legal review, or approvals may need to shift by a week.
  - If the Board meeting or other downstream deadlines are fixed, confirm whether the prep still gives the same lead time.
- Resource and logistics
  - Room reservations, catering, AV support and any recurring room bookings may need to be moved; those resources sometimes have limited availability on different weeks.
  - If external attendees travel, a different week may conflict with travel schedules or other meetings.
- People’s availability and travel patterns
  - Members who block time in the first week (e.g., “Block first Tuesday for recurring internal meetings”) may be unavailable in the second week.
  - People who are frequently traveling mid-month may be more/less available on the second Tuesday.
- Payroll/operations or reporting cycles
  - Monthly administrative tasks (invoicing, payroll cutoffs, month‑end reconciliations) sometimes have mid-month cycles—check whether any stakeholder is critical to prep and is busy on the new date.
- Perception and organizational cadence
  - Moving prep later in the month can compress or expand the window between prep and the actual board meeting (if the board meeting date is tied to the first Tuesday). That affects review cycles and follow-ups.

3) What attendees will see in their calendars and notifications
- Update to a recurring invite
  - If you update the existing recurring event to “second Tuesday,” attendees will receive an updated invitation/notification (depending on their mail/calendar settings) showing the new recurrence rule and the next occurrence on the second Tuesday.
- New conflicts/double bookings
  - Attendees whose calendars already have events at that time will see a conflict (overlap) and may receive a suggestion to accept/decline or propose a new time.
- RSVP and declines
  - People who cannot attend the new date will likely decline; organizers will see declines or tentative responses.
- Changed reminders and travel/time-zone effects
  - Reminders and any linked conferencing will remain, but reminders fire on the new date. If attendees are in other time zones or have travel that week, they may get notified more/less in advance.
- Possible appearance of both events (if you create a new recurring event rather than edit)
  - If you leave the first-Tuesday series intact and create a new second-Tuesday series, attendees could see two recurring events (old and new) until one is cancelled.

4) Quick checklist to run before you actually change it
- Inventory stakeholders: list required vs optional attendees and check their standing commitments on Tuesdays.
- Check deliverable deadlines: who must produce materials and when; shift those deadlines by a week if necessary.
- Scan for known recurring meetings on second Tuesdays (committees, vendor reviews, execs).
- Verify resource availability: rooms, AV, catering, conferencing.
- Communicate proposed change (timing and rationale) and solicit objections before editing the recurring invite.
- If you decide to change: decide whether to update the existing recurring event (notifies everyone and changes future instances) or create a new series and cancel the old one (gives a clearer history but can cause duplicate bookings briefly).
- Consider a soft pilot: propose the change for a single occurrence (one month) before switching the full recurrence.

5) Suggested next steps I can help with (no action until you say so)
- I can scan your calendars for conflicts on the second-Tuesday slot (I’d need permission to check calendars).
- I can draft a short message to attendees explaining the proposed shift and asking for conflicts or objections.
- I can produce a one-month example calendar showing the date mapping (first Tuesday → second Tuesday) for any month you pick, so you can visualize exact dates.

Would you like me to (a) draft an announcement to attendees, (b) check calendars for conflicts, or (c) produce a sample month mapping? I’ll wait for your go‑ahead—I won’t change any events yet.
